title: Span selection modes and hinting — sketches & grooming notes
content:
Purpose and problem statement:
We often need to select one or more spans inside a trace to inspect logs, copy span IDs, run quick span-level evals, or compare timing across spans. Current interactive affordances in the viewer are limited to single-span click + right panel. This doc explores a richer set of selection modes, explicit hinting (microcopy + hover affordances), and keyboard flows to speed triage and reduce accidental clicks.

Goals (success criteria):
- Enable quick multi-span comparisons without leaving trace view.
- Reduce accidental span-select by adding clear hover hints and confirmation affordances for destructive actions (delete/mark).
- Provide keyboard-first navigation and selection for power users and accessibility parity.
- Design a small persistent selection toolbar with common span actions (copy id, view logs, summarize, bookmark).

High-level proposals (selection modes):
1) Click-to-select (default): single left-click highlights a span, opens detail panel. Single selection only unless modifier used.
   - Visual: 2px accent outline + subtle lift (shadow) + timeline scrub focus.
2) Ctrl/Cmd+click multi-select: accumulate spans in selection set (order preserved). Selected spans get numeric badges (1,2,3) to indicate selection order for compare flows.
3) Shift+click range-select: picks contiguous spans in the timeline between anchor and target. Works across collapsed groups (expands temporarily).
4) Lasso/drag select: click-and-drag across waterfall to select overlapping spans in time window. Good for burst investigations.
5) Keyboard expansion: with focus on a span, press Shift+ArrowLeft/Right to expand selection to previous/next sibling span; press Enter to toggle selection.
6) Pick mode (mode toggle): a persistent toggle button in the trace toolbar to enter "pick mode" for touch/trackpad users — tap to select multiple spans without modifiers.

Hinting and microcopy rules:
+ Hover hint line: 'Click to open • Ctrl+click to compare'
+ When a user hovers for 300ms, show a small pill with primary action and shortcut (e.g., 'Open span — Enter')
+ For long spans that visually occlude others, show a small chevron "peek" on hover to reveal stacked spans beneath
+ When Ctrl/Cmd held down, change cursor and show temporary top banner: 'Compare mode — Ctrl+click to add spans'

Selection visual language and wireframe notes:
- Default state: no selection. Spans use base fill + low-contrast border.
- Hover state: 1px bright border + subtle glow. Show action pills near cursor (open/copy id).
- Selected span: 2px accent border + drop shadow + selection number badge in top-left of span rect.
- Multi-selected set: draw soft connection line above timeline linking selected spans in order to communicate compare direction (dashed connector).
- Selection toolbar: sticky row at bottom of trace viewport with actions: [Compare timings] [Copy span ids] [Summarize spans] [Open logs] [Create eval] [Pin selection]. Toolbar is hidden when selection empty.

Quick ASCII wireframe (timeline top, spans below):
[trace toolbar]  | search | filters | pick mode [ON] |
---------------- TIMELINE RULER ----------------
|  ┌──────────── span A ──────┐   ┌───── span C ─┐ |
|  |  [1] span B            |   | [2] span D    | |
|  └─────────────────────────┘   └───────────────┘ |
----------------- selection-toolbar (visible) ----------------
[ Compare timings ]  [ Copy ids ]  [ Open logs ]  [ Summarize ]
(Selection: 2 spans • total duration: 340ms)

Interaction flows (detailed):
Flow A: Fast inspect
- Mouse over span -> hover pill shows 'Open (Enter)', 'Copy id (C)'.
- Press Enter -> open right-hand panel with span timeline, tags, logs.
- Press Esc -> close panel and clear focus (not selection).

Flow B: Compare two spans
- Hold Ctrl/Cmd -> cursor changes, banner 'Compare mode'.
- Click first span -> anchor (badge 1).
- Click second span -> badge 2; selection-toolbar appears; choose 'Compare timings' to open a modal timeline diff.

Flow C: Range triage across collapsed groups
- Click span in collapsed group -> Shift+click span outside group -> auto-expand minimal set of groups to include range, select continuous set.

Keyboard nav and shortcuts (proposal):
- j / k: move focus to next/previous span (same as trace row traversal).
- Enter: open focused span.
- Space: toggle selection of focused span.
- Shift+Arrows: range-select.
- C: copy ids of current selection.
- P: pin selection (creates transient saved set in console).
- ? : show keyboard help overlay.

Accessibility considerations:
- All selection actions must be available via keyboard and have clear aria-live announcements (e.g., 'Span selected: http.handler — 72ms').
- Numeric badges must also be read by screen readers in selection order.
- Ensure focus ring color contrast meets AA.
- Provide a non-visual selection mode: 'selection list' in side panel that mirrors the selection set and supports keyboard reorder.

Telemetry & metrics to capture: (for product grooming)
- Selection type used (single, multi, range, lasso, keyboard)
- Time from first hover to first select (probe for discoverability)
- Actions taken from selection toolbar (counts of Copy, Compare, Summarize)
- Errors or accidental double-clicks (to detect accidental opens)

Backlog & grooming checklist (next steps + rough estimates):
- UX spike: interactive prototype (Figma) of selection modes — 3d
- Engineering spike: lightweight selection state + toolbar infra in trace component — 4d
- Accessibility review & ARIA passes — 2d
- Instrument telemetry events + dashboard for selections — 2d
- E2E tests: keyboard nav + selection persistence — 3d
- Rollout plan: A/B behind feature flag (experiments) — 1d
Estimated priority: P1 for power-user flows (keyboard, compare), P2 for lasso and pick-mode polish.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should numeric badges indicate selection order or click recency? (proposal: order of addition)
- Persistent saved selection semantics: should pins be global, per-user, or per-team?
- On mobile/touch, is pick-mode sufficient or do we need long-press for multi-select?
- UX for selection connectors on dense traces — do connectors add noise? fallback: condensed connector with hover reveal.

Notes from grooming meeting (2024-11-12):
- Marcus: prefer minimal visual noise; keep connectors thin and optional.
- Lina: keyboard-first flow is highest impact for support engineers.
- Engineering: prefer to ship Ctrl+click, Shift+click, keyboard nav first; lasso can be second phase.

Acceptance criteria (v0):
- Single + Ctrl+click multi-select implemented and stable.
- Selection toolbar with Copy ids and Open logs actions.
- Basic keyboard nav (j/k/Enter/Space) and ARIA announcements.
- Telemetry events for selection type and toolbar actions.
